jewelry.title: Two strings of shell disc beads. [El.B 'DCF 2004-2006 What's Upstairs?' 21/7/2005]

K'lengi mu. Silver pendant of the head of a crocodile holing a fish in its mouth. Pendant is decorated with raised spirals and pronounced features. Attached to a chain of silver links by two loops at one end of the head.

Silver wire bracelet/bangle. Circular cross-section. The two ends are flattened and wound around the opposite end to create a hoop. Separate small piece of silver wire wound around the band towards the centre.
One of three ropes of beads for the waist, made by winding a string of small glass beads of many colours round a cord of fibres. Ashembi.
String of 64 beads. Each bead is red glass and sub-cuboid, with two faces convex-sided and two concave-sided so that each bead fits closely to the adjacent beads.

One of two Gonja waistbands made mainly of shell disc beads from shells found in nearby rivers. At the place where the string is knotted are in one case a yellow cylindrical glass bead with blue, green and red "eyes".
One of three ropes of beads for the waist, made by winding a string of small glass beads of many colours round a cord of fibres. Ashembi.
One of three ropes of beads for the waist, made by winding a string of small glass beads of many colours round a cord of fibres. Ashembi.
One of two Gonja waistbands made mainly of shell disc beads from shells found in nearby rivers. At the place where the string is knotted are 4 yellow rectangular beads with red dots like dice.
Silver wire bracelet/bangle, oval. Circular cross-section. The two ends are flattened and wound around the opposite end to create a hoop.
Silver wire bracelet/bangle. Circular cross-section. The two ends are flattened and wound around the opposite end to create a hoop. Slightly tarnished.
Silver wire bracelet/bangle, slightly bent. Circular cross-section. The two ends are flattened and wound around the opposite end to create a hoop. Tarnished.
Silver wire bracelet/bangle, slightly bent. Circular cross-section. The two ends bent and tapering to points.

String of beads. 25 are red glass and sub-cuboid, with two faces convex-sided and two concave-sided so that each bead fits closely to the adjacent beads. Five are the same shape but cream-coloured. Six are the same shape but black. Three are the same shape but blue; one yellow. Four are the same shape, red and transparent. There is one cylindrical red bead. Three annular red, black and white beads. Three annular red, blue and white beads.
String of 49 beads. 46 are cylindrical coral. One is oval and possibly a pink stone (Quartz?). Two are red glass; one cylindrical, one oval.
String of seven beads. Five are carnelian; roughly cylindrical or rectangular, one flat and hexagonal. One bead is opaline glass in a narrow oval shape. One is biconical pink quartz.

ceramic.title: Red ware pottery drinking vessel for foals, with 7 oval shaped openings. [ASh [OPS move] 11/03/2016]
Kadupuli. Burnished carinated bowl of smoked buff ware with an everted flaring rim, shallow grooved band decoration below neck and a rounded base. Bowl for eating soup.
Kafitalapulia. Pottery lamp of reddish buff ware. Hemispherical bowl, solid stem flaring out into ring base; externally burnished.

Lidded pot making up a Gonja twin shrine (with 1965.39 B.1-2). (.1) Round base rising to a carinated shoulder to meet an everted rim. Decorated with a band of indentations above the shoulder. (.2)Thick lid with looped handle which was previously detached but is now re-attached.
Dawadawa. One half of a dried seed pod, roughly oval in shape. Used as a tool in pottery making for scraping the inside and outside of a pot. Clay residue remains embedded on the objects' surface.
Mborebi. Lidded pot forming half of a Gonja twin shrine (with 1965.39 A.1-2). (.1) Rounded pot with uneven rim and thick walls. (.2)Thick lid with peg handle.

Kadupuli. Globular bowl, of possible smoked buff ware, with slightly rounded base, flaring everted rim and neck featuring a band of multiple horizontal grooves. Smooth, irregular burnished finish. Bowl for eating soup.
Kaboliti. A dried and worn corn cob, cylindrical in shape and encrusted with dried clay. Used as a tool in pottery making for the initial burnishing of the outside of a vessel.

Calebasse
Spool, consisting of a wooden stick with a clay weight on one end to hold the whirl on. There is white spun cotton wound on the spool, ready to spin with.
Shallow circular woven straw basket with flat base, rising slightly in the centre internally, loosely coiled fibre rim as well as contrasting stakes and light red bands along the body.
Circular straw basket with raised middle, loosely coiled rim and bands of contrasting light red stripes along the body.
Large woven straw basket with flattened base, rising slightly in the centre internally, and a loosely coiled rim.
A container made from half of a calabash or gourd, hemispherical in shape.
A container made from half of a calabash, hemispherical in shape. The gourd vessel is decorated on the exterior with carved geometric patterns below the rim and drawings on the base.
Bag of unprocessed cotton bolls, with small pieces of plant matter.
Bag containing a piece of carded cotton, ready for spinning. There are also small black flecks of plant matter.
Small bag of cotton ready for carding and spinning.

Small leather bag containing unknown items, possibly flint (.1). The edges of the bag are sewn together with a long length of flat leather. Flap of leather covering the entrance, partially damaged and missing, animal claw pierced through the front. Twisted leather handle at the top. triangular steel striker (.2), two ends folded over at the top.
Kakpokpo. Wooden pounder used for crushing shea nuts (see 1965.26 B). One larger pounding surface and a smaller terminal on the opposite end.
Spoon made from half of a gourd or calabash. Decorated with geometric burnt designs representing Ananse, the spider and his web.

A lidded jewel box made from two halves of a calabash. The gourd container [A] is hemispherical with a rounded base. The lid [B] is hemispherical with a protruding top and is slightly smaller allowing it to fit inside. Both are decorated with controlled burn marks consisting of line and cross patterns.

Kasalankwon. Two gourd vessels associated with the drink pito. Both have a spherical body that constricts then expands to the wide mouth and both have a slightly rounded base. One is larger than the other [A].
Kawaruntfu. A lid made from half of a calabash, hemispherical in shape. Used with gourd vessels [1965.31 A-B] to drink pito or water.
Spoon made from half of a gourd or calabash. Decorated with geometric burnt designs.
Spoon made from half of a gourd or calabash. Decorated with geometric burnt designs representing Ananse, the spider and his web.

Kadibi. A carved wooden block, roughly rectangular in shape with slightly flaring ends. Used as a tool in pottery making to smooth or burnish a vessel. Fragments of dried clay are adhered to the object's surface.

Kadibi. A carved wooden paddle, flat with one rectangular end tapering to a rounded point at the other. Used as a tool in pottery making for paddling or shaping the outside of a vessel. Fragments of dried clay are adhered to the object's surface.

masks-ritual.title: Flywhisk of pale animal hair with leather covered handle. The handle is decorated with dyed leather. [MJD 06/08/2009]

instruments.title: Mpepe. Pair of rattles with gourd bases and conical tops made of red and yellow raffia basketry, partly wicker and partly twined.

textile.title: Embroidered gown.

A whirl. Consisting of a thin stick, cylindrical in shape with each end tapering to a point, fitted just above one end is a clay spherical weight. The clay ball is decorated with red and yellow stripes and a white dotted pattern at the centre on a black background. A length of cotton is tightly wound around the stick. Used in textile production to spin wool or cotton.

A whirl. Consisting of a thin stick, cylindrical in shape with each end tapering to a point, fitted just above one end is a clay biconical weight. The clay ball is decorated with a red, yellow and white striped pattern at the centre on a black background. Used in textile production to spin wool or cotton.

A whirl. Consisting of a thin stick, cylindrical in shape with each end tapering to a point, fitted just above one end is a clay spherical weight. The clay ball is decorated with a red, yellow and white striped pattern on a black background. Used in textile production to spin wool or cotton.

A wooden hand loom with some partially-woven fabric. One one side, three spools of cotton yarn in white, blue, and navy, are being threaded through the slats of the loom; there are also two wooden discs attached, as well as cotton in blue, white, and pink. On the other side, there is a strip of blue and white striped fabric. The end of the strip is wound round a long wooden pole with holes drilled through at one end.
A thin stick, cylindrical in shape with each end tapering to a point. Possibly part of a whirl for use in textile production. One end has white marks, possibly paint.
A thin stick, cylindrical in shape with each end tapering to a point. Possibly part of a whirl for use in textile production.
A piece of bamboo, hollow and cylindrical in shape with two roughly cut ends. Used in textile production for winding cotton.
A piece of bamboo, cylindrical in shape with one straight cut end and one irregular end. Used in textile production for winding cotton.
A piece of wood, cylindrical in shape with one rounded end and one roughly cut end. Used in textile production as part of a weaving apparatus; signs of wear on the objects' surface.

A whirl for spinning cotton. It consists of a thin wooden stick, with a spherical clay weight at one end. The weight is painted black with three narrow white stripes. A small amount of white and red cotton thread has been wound around the stick.

A whirl for spinning cotton. It consists of a thin wooden stick, pointed at one end with a clay weight at the other end. The weight is painted black with narrow white stripes. White cotton thread has been wound around the stick.
A piece of white chalk used for marking cloth in dressmaking.
Long piece of woven cotton wound up [A]. Blue and white check pattern. Possibly many lengths of cloth wound together; with one  length separate from bundle [B].
Sample of woven cotton fabric with light blue, dark blue and white stripe.
Sample of woven cotton fabric in stripes of red, white, blue, red, yellow and black.
Sample of woven cotton fabric with narrow stripes in blue, white and light blue.

Woven cotton piece of fabric with dark blue, cream and light blue stripe with three red stripes, one on the edge of the cloth. On top of the basic striped fabric are geometric designs woven in orange, cream and yellow. Badly torn in centre.

Woven cotton piece of fabric with blue, light blue, red and white stripe; blue stripes thick, red and white thin. Diamond and rectangular shapes woven into the fabric, on top of the basic stripe design. Worn in several places, frayed edges.
Woven cotton cloth with raised stripe. Cream coloured fabric. Bottom and top edges frayed.
Square piece of cotton fabric. Dark blue background with white and blue motifs created by tie-dye method.
Large rectangular piece of dark blue cotton fabric with tie-dye lines and circles in white. The lines are tied so as to form squares.

Small rectangular piece of dark blue cotton. Five pieces of cord are sewn into the fabric, length-wise giving the fabric a raised stripe on one side. Presumably the cords would be pulled out and the fabric would have a white stripe.
Long piece of dark blue cotton with cord sewn in diagonally. Presumably this will give the fabric a white stripe if taken out.
Fabric. Plain piece of undyed cotton prepared for tie-dyeing. The fabric has been raised in ridges to form squares, and, small circular pieces to form circles when dyed. Good condition. Whole.
A small piece of cylindrical and hollow bamboo. Used in textile production as part of a weaving apparatus.
A whirl weight. Made from clay and spherical in shape with a perforated hole through the centre. Black in colour and decorated with horizontal white stripes.

Whirl for spinning cotton. It consists of a thin wooden stick, pointed at one end, with a domed clay weight at the other end that has been painted black and white. The stick has been wound with white cotton thread.

A whirl. Consisting of a thin stick, cylindrical in shape with each end tapering to a point, fitted just above one end is a clay biconical weight. The clay ball is decorated with a red, yellow and white striped pattern at the centre on a black background. The wooden end near the weight has broken away. Used in textile production to spin wool or cotton.

Ngbanyawaja cloth with a Daboya pattern. Strips of woven cotton cloth with 15 alternating stripes of dark blue, blue and white. White bands in the weft. Unhemmed; Nine single strips and three double strips held together by a few threads.
A whirl weight. Made from clay and spherical in shape with a perforated hole through the centre. Black in colour and decorated with horizontal white stripes, now faded.
A whirl weight. Made from clay and spherical in shape with a perforated hole through the centre. White in colour and decorated with horizontal purple stripes, now faded.
A whirl weight. Made from clay and spherical in shape with a perforated hole through the centre. White in colour and decorated with horizontal purple stripes, now faded.

garment.title: Tunic of woven blue and white cotton with yellow embroidered patterns around the chest on the front and reverse. Wide sleeves with triangular neckline.
Small hand sewn tunic, possibly a child's dress. The tunic is made from a blue and white striped fabric that is pleated from the waist. The arm and neck openings are open.

Tunic/Dress of woven cotton with v-neck, wide dark blue and white stripe, decorated with coloured geometric shapes. Front panel in green, pink and cream triangles, those on the right elongated and horizontal. Back panel in green, pink, lilac and mauve triangles and diamonds. Pleated in triangular pleats from the waist. Hand stitched, badly torn.

Tunic of woven cotton with dark blue, light blue and white stripes, machine stitched and lined with cream cotton. It has a round neckline with a small slit at the bottom, decorated with a thick band of white satin finish cotton thread. The upper part of the tunic is straight from shoulder to hem with open armholes to the waist. The lower part flares out with pleats from the waist.

Pair of wide trousers hand-sewn from woven cotton with narrow dark blue, mid blue and white stripes, with lighter stripes woven horizontally to give the effect of a check. Plain blue waistband with a drawstring cord. Gathered cuffs at the ankles, with lots of fabric in the middle that would be gathered when worn. Frayed round waist band and legs.
Apron or sash made from a blue and white striped woven cotton fabric. Triangular shape with long, wide white piece of woven cotton attached to the square end.
Small blue and white stripe hat made from woven cotton. Lined with beige and pink silk fabric. Hand sewn.

Hat, hand-sewn from woven cotton fabric. It has a dark blue, mid blue and white striped pattern, with fainter white stripes woven in perpendicular to the other stripes to create a checked design. It is lined with cream cotton fabric.
Hat of woven, blue and white cotton creating a chequered patterned surface. The lining is beige cotton.

Hat, hand-sewn from woven cotton fabric, with dark blue, light blue and white stripes. Lighter white stripe woven in perpendicular to the other stripes to create a checked design. Hat is lined with cream cotton fabric.

Child's waist belt of brown, black and white leather. Closed in with a sliding slip knot style join; alternating brown and white leather on either side of a rectangular piece of leather decoration with shallow punch marks and diagonal lines in darker staining.

sculpture.title: Wooden figure of a woman carrying a child on her left hip. She has pierced ears, a distinctive hairstyle, a scarification mark on her cheek and is wearing a red bead necklace.

A male figure carved from wood. The face is marked with linear and cross scarifications on each cheek. The figure is standing upright on an integral base. The proper right hand is raised to the ear and the other arm is held at the side and wears a bracelet. Stained light brown and with a highly polished finish.
Carved wooden male figure standing on a square base with a staff in his right hand. His left arm is down by his side. Linear incisions suggest a domed hairstyle. Left thumb is chipped.

metalwork.title: Kwari. A metal pottery scraper with a curved and roughly rectangular plate for scraping that tapers to a band forming a bracelet like shape. Fragments of dried clay are adhered to the object's surface. Used as a tool in pottery making to scrape the inside of a pot.
